title: fix(gateway): keep manual recovery when restart triage declines
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes foreground Gateways exiting after an in-process restart refuses configuration and automatic triage declines, removing the operator's signal-based recovery path.

## User Impact

A declined triage keeps the process alive and prints the startup refusal, Doctor command, and applicable recovery step. Unmanaged runs also remain available for manual recovery after an admitted triage failure or failed startup retry. Recorded supervisors retain the nonzero-exit recovery path. Windows and external supervisors receive their own restart instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart recovery owner treated every outcome other than `completed` as terminal. It now distinguishes a declined handoff from a confirmed, admitted triage failure and uses the run loop's existing supervisor identity to decide whether exiting can recover the Gateway. Successful triage still gets one startup retry after confirmed cleanup. Startup cleanup and cancellation barriers remain intact, and the updater's return contract is preserved.

Recovery messages live with the existing startup-recovery owner; `run-loop.ts` shrinks by two lines. The exit contract is documented in `docs/cli/triage.md`. This changes restart recovery without changing configuration, storage schemas, dependencies, or updater backup/rollback behavior.

Refs #159539, #160173

## Evidence

- Baseline `42700f9d92dc8bc127ba31c634d90230b9b2b18e`: four recovery cases failed because the loop terminated; the real continuation test also failed because an admitted failure was returned as declined.
- Linux Testbox live proof through `pnpm openclaw gateway run`, with isolated state, a free loopback port, and no supervisor markers: HTTP 200 → refused `gateway.bind` → PID 12786 alive with no HTTP listener and visible `openclaw doctor --fix` / `kill -USR2 12786` guidance → corrected config plus SIGUSR2 → HTTP 200 in the same PID after 2.08 seconds → SIGTERM exit 0. Only the task-owned Gateway was signaled.
- Touched suites passed three times on the final source: one importer run and two focused repetitions (268 tests per touched-suite pass). The 13 importer suites passed 486 tests, with one existing macOS-only skip on Linux. Importer run wall time: 237.99 seconds; focused repetition wall times: 129.59 and 108.79 seconds.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <all changed paths>` passed on Testbox: all 27 test typecheck graphs, core typechecking, formatting, lint, line-cap ratchet, unused-export scans, and repository guards. Wall time: 1775.18 seconds. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh direct-route Codex autoreview at P1: scoped-clean. Windows guidance was corrected after the first review finding. A queued mock startup in the new regression fixture was corrected; no retries or weaker assertions were added.

With `--maxWorkers=1`, the final focused repetition measured 33.01 seconds wall / approximately 31.4 seconds test time for the run-loop and startup-triage pair, 8.79 / 6.9 seconds for the real continuation failure fixture, and 63.98 / 36.5 seconds for the continuation lifecycle suite. Compilation is included only in wall time. The existing lifecycle suites exercise signal ordering, cleanup, ownership, and real child-process settlement; new run-loop cases use completion events. No individual test exceeded 30 seconds or file exceeded 120 seconds of test time. Windows guidance has unit coverage; live proof was Linux.

Production: +69/-19 lines. Tests and test support: +112/-30. Docs: +5/-1. Validation used local/Testbox proof; no CI reruns were requested. Auto-merge remains off.
